subject: Oceanography
title: Polar Plankton Blooms
description: A micro-lesson that makes Polar Plankton Blooms usable.

hook.text: When polar ice melts in spring, the ocean beneath explodes with life—one of Earth's greatest biological events.

buildup.text: Sunlight reaches water previously shaded by ice—nutrients accumulated over winter fuel explosive growth.

discovery.text: Phytoplankton blooms can double their biomass daily—visible as green swirls in satellite images.

twist.text: Climate change is making blooms earlier—mismatching timing with zooplankton and fish that depend on them.

climax.text: This mismatch can ripple through food webs—seabirds arrive to find food already gone.

punchline.text: Spring blooms feed the polar world—but timing is everything.

quiz.question: What causes polar plankton blooms?
options: Sunlight reaches nutrient-rich water when ice melts
Warm currents arrive from the tropics
